title: Progressive Cohort-Based Exposure Controller for Model Version Experiments
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: Build a first-class A/B experiment controller that lets teams run stratified cohort experiments across model versions with progressive exposure, shadow routing, and automatic statistical checks and rollback triggers. The controller should be available as both a Console workflow (experiment creation UI) and a config-driven API for infra/CI-driven experiments. Core use-cases: canary rollouts, multi-variant A/B tests, long-running quality experiments with shadow traffic, and automatic rollback when predefined safety/regression thresholds are breached.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console: create experiment with cohort definitions (percent, attributes), target routes, model variants, and schedule. 2) API: create/edit/stop experiment via REST with JSON schema. 3) Exposure controls: support progressive ramps, hold durations, and emergency pause. 4) Stats: real-time cohort metrics (latency, token cost, perplexity/quality proxy, error rates) and a significance test (two-sample proportion or bootstrap for custom metrics). 5) Auto-rollback: configurable thresholds (regression delta and p-value) that trigger automated rollback and incident record. 6) Shadowing: ability to send 100% shadow traffic to variant for offline comparison without affecting responses. 7) Docs & runbook published; smoke tests and end-to-end test coverage added.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight controller service that orchestrates routing policies held in Smart Routing. The controller will generate per-route policy objects: cohort definitions, routing weights, and guard rails. It will emit events to telemetry and to the Console UI. Statistical checks implemented as a pluggable service: default tests are two-sample bootstrap for generative quality metrics and Mann-Whitney U for continuous signals; we will add support for custom evaluation functions. Auto-rollback is a policy that invokes routing change + incident creation + optional webhook to customer infra. Interaction with Dedicated and Private: controller must validate model compatibility (quantization/latency) via model catalog metadata. Backfill work required in ENG-48211 for continuous batching metrics and ENG-49820 for KV cache telemetry.
telemetry_and_metrics: Minimum required metrics: per-cohort request count, median latency (p50/p95), token cost per request, model error rate (5xx/timeout), quality proxy (BLEU/perplexity/embedding-similarity vs baseline), user-visible degradation events. Derived stats: per-cohort uplift/delta and confidence interval, p-value for regression. Dashboards: per-experiment overview, cohort time-series, early-warning alerts for drift and quota burn. Storage: keep experiment-level aggregates at 1m granularity for 30 days, 1h thereafter.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): API and basic Console flow, cohort weight routing, simple z-test for binary metrics, shadow traffic plumbing. Phase 2 (2 sprints): progressive ramp UI, bootstrap tests for non-parametric signals, auto-rollback integration, runbook. Phase 3 (1 sprint): Dedicated/Private validation, performance tuning, GA documentation and example templates. Initial canary template: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% with hold periods and automatic stop on regression. All ramps are configurable per-experiment.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives from noisy metrics causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require minimum sample sizes and allow configurable lookback windows; default use conservative thresholds and paired tests where possible. Risk: latency spikes during progressive ramps due to model cold starts. Mitigation: warmup runs and shadow priming before route weight change. Risk: security/compliance for Private customers. Mitigation: local controller mode with no metadata exfiltration and optional KMS key gating for telemetry exports.
